strongest_angle: Analyze the James Webb Space Telescope's observation of the IC 348 star cluster, detailing the discovery of record-breaking low-mass brown dwarfs with masses down to 3 to 4 times that of Jupiter.

key_facts.fact: The James Webb Space Telescope identified a record-breaking free-floating brown dwarf in the IC 348 star cluster with a mass of 3 to 4 times that of Jupiter.
Located 1,000 light-years from Earth in the Perseus constellation, the IC 348 young star cluster was targeted by astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope.
Researchers used the NIRSpec spectrograph on the James Webb Space Telescope to obtain spectra of brown dwarf candidates in the IC 348 cluster.
The faintest confirmed brown dwarf in IC 348 has an estimated mass of 3 to 4 times the mass of Jupiter, representing the least massive brown dwarf confirmed with spectroscopy.
